subject: sociology

items.q: Do official statistics record all crime accurately?
items.correct: No — much crime is unreported or unrecorded (the 'dark figure').
items.random_wrong: Everyone has an equal chance of being caught.
items.why: Crime statistics are socially constructed; many crimes never reach the records.

items.q: Is crime spread evenly across all social groups?
items.correct: No — recorded crime and policing vary by class, age, ethnicity and area.
items.misconception: Yes, all groups commit and are caught equally.
items.random_wrong: Only statistics decide who is a criminal.
items.why: Patterns in statistics reflect both behaviour and how society/police respond.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Sociology (0495) syllabus; Crime, Deviance & Social Control
